messages:
michael: short follow-up from last night's postmortem. We observed recurring throughput falls when long-run batches hit node-group B. We need owners for remediation, a short-term SLO guardrail, and dashboarding for burst patterns.

leah: noted. I instrumented request-size histograms and saw spikes aligning with customers using seq>2048 and batch_size>16. link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/throughput-bursts (heatmap) :mag_right:

oscar: upstream infra reported IO stalls ~3s on the same nodes. could be noisy neighbor on shared NVMe. I'll correlate node IDs and attach disk metrics. ETA 24h.

tess: For SLOs, propose we keep the published SLA but add a temporary operational SLO: "99th latency for critical-cust-tier must remain <350ms for 30d". For non-critical tiers, add a burst-protection throttle at 2x baseline. This avoids exposing customers to rolling SLA edits.

michael: I like the operational SLO as a safety valve. Who owns implementing the throttle and gating rollout?

leah: I can add a per-tenant throttle hook in the router and expose a feature flag for a 2-week canary. ETA 48h for the flag + basic tests.

oscar: I'll produce the node-to-IO correlation table and suggest a mitigant (node cordon + evict noisy pods) if disk latency >10ms sustained. ETA 12h.

alertbot: Incident 2026-03-20: tagged as recurring-throughput-burst and linked to PM-5150.

tess: Also propose alert thresholds: 7d error-budget burn at 60% -> Eng-oncall notify; 7d burn at 90% -> open remediation sprint + pause non-critical rollouts. Add a dashboard panel for rolling-7d and projected burn.

michael: Action items and owners: 1) Router throttle + flag (leah) 2) Node IO correlation + mitigation list (oscar) 3) Rolling-7d burn panel + projected burn sim (tess) 4) Customer comms template (michael). Target: all items staged in a branch within 72h, canary enabled in 96h.

leah: probe query I'll add to the new panel:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, model))
```

oscar: quick note 1 1: found a batch of pods on node-42 with sustained iowait 120s window. I'll start an evict test on a single node tomorrow and report.

tess: I'll draft the internal note for support and AMs so they can respond to customers if they see throttling. michael, can you review before EOD?

michael: Yup I'll review. Let's meet Fri 09:30 PT to verify canary metrics and decide on wider rollout. If the canary reduces 99p for critical tier by >20%, we proceed. If not, we revert and escalate to infra for hardware investigation.

leah: noted. I'll also add a synthetic that simulates long sequence load to validate throttle behavior.

michael: Thanks team. I'll update the postmortem action tracker with these owners and timelines. Ping here with any blockers. :thumbsup:
